item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"Candidate B is substantially more faithful to the frozen contract because Upload delegates directly to FilesService.Add after creating the replayable multipart body.","reasons":["B reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile with the required field name \"file\" and supplied filename.","B routes the encoded body through s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...), exactly preserving established option handling, request construction, decoding, and error semantics.","A instead duplicates Add's option processing, POST request, payload decoding, and missing-data handling, directly violating the explicit reuse requirement and creating future drift risk.","Both preserve Add and validate empty filename or nil content before constructing a request and propagate NewFile reader errors unchanged."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates substantial FilesService.Add machinery despite the contract requiring delegation through Add.","Its detailed changelog and comments expose transport implementation details and make broad retry claims that add maintenance burden.","Visible tests omit validation and source-reader failure cases required by the contract."],"risks_b":["Visible tests omit validation and source-reader failure cases required by the contract.","The retry test uses strings.NewReader directly rather than a wrapped or otherwise streamed reader, so it does not clearly demonstrate the reported non-replayable-source scenario.","The exported Upload method lacks a Go documentation comment."]}
